From e76239fed3cffd6d304d8ca3ce23984fd24f57d3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:48:53 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: ccp: Don't attempt to copy PDH cert to userspace if
 PSP command failed

When retrieving the PDH cert, don't attempt to copy the blobs to userspace
if the firmware command failed.  If the failure was due to an invalid
length, i.e. the userspace buffer+length was too small, copying the number
of bytes _firmware_ requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and
leak data to userspace.

Reported-by: Sebastian Alba Vives <sebasjosue84@gmail.com>
Fixes: 76a2b524a4b1 ("crypto: ccp: Implement SEV_PDH_CERT_EXPORT ioctl command")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

diff --git a/drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c b/drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c
index 86c6858a5c18..e4c7c2a6fe55 100644
--- a/drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c
+++ b/drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c
@@ -2339,7 +2339,10 @@ static int sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export(struct sev_issue_cmd *argp, bool writable)
 
 	ret = __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_PDH_CERT_EXPORT, &data, &argp->error);
 
-	/* If we query the length, FW responded with expected data. */
+	/*
+	 * Firmware will return the length of the blobs (either the minimum
+	 * required length or the actual length written), return 'em to the user.
+	 */
 	input.cert_chain_len = data.cert_chain_len;
 	input.pdh_cert_len = data.pdh_cert_len;
 
@@ -2348,6 +2351,9 @@ static int sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export(struct sev_issue_cmd *argp, bool writable)
 		goto e_free_cert;
 	}
 
+	if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error))
+		goto e_free_cert;
+
 	if (pdh_blob) {
 		if (copy_to_user(input_pdh_cert_address,
 				 pdh_blob, input.pdh_cert_len)) {

2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c`

#### Changes:
1. **Updated comment** (line 2342–2345):  
   Replaced a misleading comment (“If we query the length, FW responded with expected data.”) with an explanation that firmware returns the length of the blobs, which should be passed back to the user regardless of the command’s success/failure.

2. **Added check after retrieving lengths** (lines 2354–2357):  
   ```c
   if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error))
       goto e_free_cert;
   ```  
   This ensures that if the PSP command failed (`ret != 0`) or the firmware returned an error (`argp->error != 0`), the function jumps directly to freeing memory **before** attempting to copy any blob data to userspace.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The comment update clarifies that the length fields are intentionally retrieved and copied to userspace even before the command’s outcome is known, because they represent either the required or actual blob sizes.
- The added conditional check is the core fix: it prevents the subsequent `copy_to_user()` calls (on lines 2357–2374) from being executed when the firmware command failed. Previously, the code continued to copy data based on the length returned by the firmware, which could be larger than the kernel-allocated buffer if the failure was due to an insufficient buffer size. This would cause a **slab-out-of-bounds read** and potential **data leak** to userspace. The new logic ensures that after retrieving the length values, any failure aborts the operation before any copying takes place.
